messages:
liam: Poked at the dedicated-pool saturation problem again. Proposal: an "admit gateway" that sits before pool admission and can route requests to fallbacks when the pool is congested. The gateway must be fast (<=1ms decision) and avoid causing a retry stampede. Thoughts?

nora: Love the gateway. Two immediate concerns: 1) how do we signal different fallback policies per-customer (enterprise may disable hosted fallback), 2) how do we communicate state so load balancers don't keep sending traffic?

diego: For (1) store allowlist/denylist in control plane; runtime subscribes. For (2) gateway should publish a small health signal + token burn rate. Also implement a per-tenant smooth-stagger: when flipping to fallback, spread admits across tenants using consistent-hash buckets over a short ramp.

sophie: Agree on consistent-hash staggering. Also propose a circuit-breaker with three states: CLOSED (normal), PROBING (allow small % through), OPEN (fallback only). Transition triggers: pool-wide queue length, p95 latency, and free-GPU slots metric.

liam: Draft config sketch:
```
admit_gateway:
  triggers:
    queue_len: 1000
    p95_ms: 250
  circuit:
    probe_rate: 0.02        # fraction allowed in PROBING
    probe_duration_s: 20
    open_min_s: 60
  tenant_stagger:
    buckets: 128
    ramp_s: 40
  fallback_policy: [private_quant, hosted_api, enqueue]
```

nora: Make fallback_policy overridable per-tenant via control plane. Also need audit field for decisions (why we redirected).

diego: On the "why" field: put a short code and human message in trace/span. Example: `ADB01 - pool-saturated -> routed(hosted_api)` so ops can filter.

sophie: Ops checklist for canary: deploy admit-gateway to 1 pool, enable PROBING only, monitor rejected_admits, latency of fallbacks, and tenant error rates. Keep an immediate rollback path that sets gateway to PASS-THROUGH.

ops-bot: infra-bot: Canary started: admit-gateway:v0.9 on pool-us-west-1 at 1716669000 :rocket:

liam: We also need a soft-throttle alternative to hard redirect: return 202 + retry-after header and enqueue request for later processing. This is useful for batchy tenants that prefer eventual completion. Add per-tenant preference: immediate_redirect|enqueue_with_retry.

nora: Good point. Add `prefer_eventual` flag on tenant config. For enqueue we must surface queue position and ETA in the API response.

diego: Implementation note: keep decision logic in the runtime process (low-latency) but make it consult a versioned policy blob from control plane. Control plane handles per-tenant overrides and rollout percent. Runtime should cache and validate signatures.

sophie: Telemetry: emit metrics: admit_decisions_total{path=[pool,hosted,enqueue], tenant, decision_code}, admit_latency_ms, probe_accept_rate, fallback_latency_by_path. Tracing: tag span with decision_code and policy_version.

liam: Security/enterprise constraints: allow customers to declare allowed_fallbacks. Enforce in control plane and runtime (runtime MUST honor denylist even if global policy tries to use path).

nora: Edge case: what if hosted_api fallback itself is overloaded and returns 503? Gateway should have short-circuit for repeated failures to that path and escalate to next fallback. That's where per-path health checks and short-term penalty windows come in.

diego: Right. Strategy: per-path health score TTLed; if failures > threshold within window, mark path degraded for penalty_s seconds and don't select it. Emit reason code (e.g., PATH_DOWN_HOSTED).

ops-bot: deploy-bot: Canary metrics baseline: no increase in pool error rate after 10m.

sophie: Next steps: 1) I'll write a runbook (canary playbook + rollback). 2) Liam will author an RFC with config API + telemetry. 3) Diego will prototype the tenant-stagger algorithm and probe state machine. 4) Nora will work with control-plane on policy distribution + per-tenant denylist.

liam: Thanks. Let's keep decisions lightweight and observable. If anyone wants to pair on the RFC/pseudo code ping me. :thumbsup:
